title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $C$ be a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over an infinite field $k$. Then the moduli stack 
$Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ of rank $n$ semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant $L$ on $C$ is $\#A^1$-connected iff it admits a $k$-rational point.

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $C$ be a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve of genus $\geq 2$ over an infinite field $k$ with $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. Let $L\in {\rm Pic}(C)$ and $n\geq 1$. Then 
    the moduli stack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ of rank $n$ semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant $L$ on $C$ admits a $k$-rational point and hence is $\#A^1$-connected.

label: def:A1-conn
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:A1-conn}
    Let $\@X$ be a simplicial presheaf on ${\rm Sm}/k$. Define ${\bm \pi}^{\mathbb A^1}_0(\@X)$, \emph{the sheaf of $\#A^1$-connected components of $\@X$}, as the Nisnevich sheafification of the presheaf  on ${\rm Sm}/k$ $$U\mapsto [U, \@X]_{\mathbb A^1}$$ 
    for each $U\in {\rm Sm}/k$. 

    We say $\@X$ is $\#A^1$-connected if the Nisnevich  sheaf ${\bm \pi}^{\mathbb A^1}_0(\@X)=*.$

label: def:naive-A1
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:naive-A1}
    Let $\@X$ be a simplicial presheaf on ${\rm Sm}/k$. Let $U$ be a $k$-scheme. Let $f_0, f_1\in \@X(U)_0$ be $0$-simplices of $\@X(U)$. We say $f_0, f_1$ are naively $\#A^1$-homotopic if there is $h: \#A^1_U\to \@X$ such that $h(0)=f_0$ and $h(1)=f_1.$

label: lem:modify-1-family

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U\subset \#A^1_K$ be the semistable locus of $\@E$, so that by assumption, $0\in U$ and $\@E|_{C\times U}$ is semistable family. 
    This corresponds to $h: U\to Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$. By \cite[Proposition 6]{Langton75} (see also \cite[Theorem 3.7]{ABBLT}), the moduli stack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ is universally closed, hence the morphism $h$ extends to a morphism (not-necessarily unique) $\-h: \#A^1_K-\{1\}\to Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$.     The morphism    $\-h$ corresponds to semistable vector bundle $\~{\@E}$ on  $C\times (\#A^1_K-\{1\})$  such that there is an isomorphism $$\phi: \~{\@E}|_{C\times U}\simeq  \@E|_{C\times U}.$$ 
We glue $(\@E|_{C\times (U\cup \{1\})}, C\times (U\cup \{1\}))$ and $(\~{\@E}, C\times (\#A^1_K-\{1\}))$ along the intersection $$(C\times (U\cup \{1\})) \cap (C\times (\#A^1_K-\{1\}))= C\times U $$ via the isomorphism $\phi$, to get the desired vector bundle $\~{\@E}$ on  $C\times \#A^1_K$.

label: lem:modif-2-family
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:modif-2-family}


Let $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal F$ be two  vector bundles on $C\times \#A^1_K$  where $U\subset \#A^1_K$ is the semistable locus of $\@E$  such that 
\[
\-E=i_1^{*}(\mathcal E) = i_0^{*}(\mathcal F)=\-F.
\] 
Assume that $0\in U$ and $1\notin U$. 
Then there is a semistable bundle $\~{\@E}$ and a bundle (not-necessarily semistable) $\~{\@F}$ on $C\times \#A^1_K$ such that   

\begin{enumerate}
\item $i_1^{*}(\~{\@E}) = i_0^{*}(\~{\@F}).$ 

    \item $\~{\@E}|_{C\times U}= \@E|_{C\times U}$ 

\item $\~{\@F}|_{C\times \{1\}}= \@F|_{C\times \{1\}}$ 

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove this in a sequence of steps. 

\medskip
\noindent
{\bf Step 1 - Elementary modification of first family :} 
Applying ~\Cref{lem:modify-1-family} to $\@E$ we get $\~{\@E}$ such that its semistable locus is equal to $\#A^1-\{1\}$ satisfying   
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\-E=i_1^{*}(\~{\@E}) = i_0^{*}(\mathcal F)=\-F$
\item $\~{\@E}$ is semistable on  $C\times (\#A^1_K-\{1\})$ 
    \item $\~{\@E}|_{C\times U}= \@E|_{C\times U}.$ 
    
\end{enumerate}
For the rest of the proof, it is enough to replace $\@E$ by $\~{\@E}$ as above.

By our assumption $\-E$ is unstable. Let $R_1$ be the local ring of $\#A^1_K$ at 1, which will be used to modify $\@E$, and let us denote by $R_0$ as the local ring of $\#A^1_K$ at 0 for $\@F$, hence $R$ (= either $R_0$ or $R_1$) is a DVR.

Let us denote by $E=i^*\@E$ for $i: C\times {\rm Spec \,} R\to C\times \#A^1_K$ and $F=i^*\@F$ for $i: C\times {\rm Spec \,} R\to C\times \#A^1_K$. We denote by $\-E$ (and $\-F$) the restriction of $E$ (and $F$) to the closed fiber $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1$ (and $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0$ respectively.)  
Note that by our assumption $\-E=\-F.$


\medskip
\noindent
{\bf Step 2 - Simultaneous elementary modification : }\\
By assumption,  $\-E$ is not semistable. Following the notation from~\cite{Langton75},   let $\-B$ be the $\beta$-subbundle of $\-E.$ We consider the exact sequence $$0\to \-B\to \-E\to \-Q\to 0$$  
Let $E^{(1)}=\ker (E\to \-E\to \-Q)$. Let us denote by $F^{(1)}=\ker (F\to \-F=\-E\to \-Q)$. 

Note that $E^{(1)}$ (and $F^{(1)}$) is a locally free sheaf on $C_{R_1}$  (and on $C_{R_0}$ resp.) such that the  restriction of $E^{(1)}$ (and $F^{(1)}$) to the closed fiber $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1$ (and $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0$ respectively) satisfies  $\-{E^{(1)}}=\-{F^{(1)}}.$ 

Now let  $\-{B^{(1)}}$ be the $\beta$-subbundle of $\-{E^{(1)}}.$ We consider the exact sequence $$0\to \-{B^{(1)}}\to\-{E^{(1)}}\to \-{Q^{(1)}}\to 0$$  
 We define $E^{(2)}=\ker (E^{(1)}\to \-{E^{(1)}}\to \-{Q^{(1)}})$ and  $F^{(2)}=\ker (F^{(1)}\to \-{F^{(1)}}=\-{E^{(1)}}\to \-{Q^{(1)}}.)$
As before note that $E^{(2)}$ (and $F^{(2)}$) is a locally free sheaf on $C_{R_1}$  (and on $C_{R_0}$ resp.) such that the  restriction of $E^{(1)}$ (and $F^{(1)}$) to the closed fiber $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1$ (and $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0$ respectively) satisfies    $\-{E^{(2)}}=\-{F^{(2)}}.$
 
Continuing this way for each $m\geq 1$, we get a sequence $\{E^{(m)}\}$ (and $\{F^{(m)}\}$) of locally free sheaves on $C_{R_1}$  (and on $C_{R_0}$, resp.) such that the  restriction of $E^{(m)}$ (and $F^{(m)}$, resp.) to the closed fiber $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1$ (and $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K\hookrightarrow C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0$ respectively) satisfies    $\-{E^{(m)}}=\-{F^{(m)}}.$ 

By \cite{Langton75} for $m$ large enough,  $\{E^{(m)}\}$ extends $E_{{\rm Frac} R}$ on $C\times {\rm Spec \,} {\rm Frac} R$ and its restriction to the closed fiber $\-{E^{(m)}} $ ( $=\-{F^{(m)}}$) is semistable.  

We fix such $m$. We can extend $E^{(m)}$ on $C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1$ to $\@E_1$ on $C\times U_1$ for a Zariski open neighbourhood $U_1$ of 1 and also  $\@F_0$ on $C\times V_0$ for a Zariski open neighbourhood $V_0$ of 0 such that \begin{enumerate}
    \item $\@E_1|_{C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1}= E^{(m)}|_{C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_1}$ 
    \item $\@E_1|_{C\times (U_1-\{1\})}\simeq  \@E|_{C\times (U_1-\{1\})}$ 
    \item $\@F_0|_{C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0}= F^{(m)}|_{C\times {\rm Spec \,} R_0}$ 
    \item $\@F_0|_{C\times (V_0-\{0\})}\simeq  \@E|_{C\times (V_0-\{0\})}$  and
    \item $\@E_1|_{C\times \{1\}}=\@F_0|_{C\times \{0\}}.$
\end{enumerate}

\noindent
{\bf Step 3 - Construction of $\~{\@E}$ :}\\
Let us write $U_0=\#A^1_K-\{1\}$. Then $\{U_0, U_1\}$ is a Zariski open cover of $C\times \#A^1_K$ such that $U_0\cap U_1=U_1-\{1\}$. Via the isomorphism from (2), $$(\@E_1)|_{C\times (U_1\cap U_0)}\simeq (\@E|_{C\times U_0})|_{C\times (U_0\cap U_1)}$$ induced by $$\@E_1|_{C\times (U_1-\{1\})}\simeq  \@E|_{C\times (U_1-\{1\})}$$ we glue $(U_0, \@E|_{U_0})$ and $(U_1, \@E_1)$  to get a locally free sheaf $\~{\@E}$ on $C\times \#A^1_K$ with desired properties. 

\medskip 
\noindent 
{\bf Step 4 - Construction of $\~{\@F}$ :}\\ 
Similarly we construct $\~{\@F}$. Let us write $V_1=\#A^1_K-\{0\}$. Then $\{V_0, V_1\}$ is a Zariski open cover of $C\times \#A^1_K$ such that $V_0\cap V_1=V_0-\{0\}$. Via the isomorphism from (4), $$(\@F_0)|_{C\times (V_0\cap V_1)}\simeq (\@F|_{C\times V_1})|_{C\times (V_1\cap V_0)}$$ induced by $$\@F_0|_{C\times (V_0-\{0\})}\simeq  \@F|_{C\times (V_0-\{0\})}$$ we glue $(V_1, \@E|_{V_1})$ and $(V_0, \@F_0)$  to get a locally free sheaf $\~{\@F}$ on $C\times \#A^1_K$ with desired properties.

label: thm:main-text-ss
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main-text-ss} Let $C$ be a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over an infinite field $k$. Then the moduli stack 
$Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ of rank $n$ semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant $L$ on $C$ is $\#A^1$-connected iff it admits a $k$-rational point.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ is $\#{A}^1$-connected. Then by \cite[Remark 2.5, page 106]{MV99}, the moduli stack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$  admits a $K$-rational point for any finitely generated field extension $K$ over $k$ (for this we note that for such $K$, ${\rm Spec \,} K$ is a Henselian local scheme).

    For the converse, we note that as $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}(k) \neq \emptyset$, then $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}(K) \neq \emptyset$ for any finitely generated field extension $K$ over $k$. 
    By~\Cref{lem:a1-chain-a1-conn}, it is enough show the following: let $K$ be a finitely generated field extension of $k.$ 
Let $E_0$ and $E_1$ be two semistable bundles on $C\times \#A^1_K$. Then there exists a chain of semistable bundles parametrized by $\mathbb A^1_K$ connecting $E_0$ and $E_1$. 

As shown in~\cite{HY24}, $E_0$ and $E_1$ are connected by a chain of bundles, say $\@E_1, \dots, \@E_r$  parametrized by $\#A^1_K$. We show that there exists a chain of semistable bundles parametrized by $\mathbb A^1_K$ connecting $E_0$ and $E_1$. We show this by induction on $r,$ the length of the $\#A^1$-chain. 

    Assume $r=1$. Let $U\subset \#A^1_K$ be the semistable locus of $\@E$ so that $0, 1\in U$ and $\@E|_{C\times U}$ is semistable family. 
    This corresponds to $h: U\to Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$. By \cite[Proposition 6]{Langton75} (see also \cite[Theorem 3.7]{ABBLT}), the moduli stack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ is universally closed, hence the morphism $h$ extends to a morphism (not-necessarily unique) $\-h: \#A^1_K\to Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$.     The morphism    $\-h$ corresponds to semistable vector bundle $\~{\@E}$ on  $C\times \#A^1_K$  such that $$\~{\@E}|_{C\times U}= \@E|_{C\times U}$$ and 
    $$\~{\@E}|_{C\times 0}= E_0 \ \ \text{and} \ \ \~{\@E}|_{C\times 1}= E_1.$$

    Assume $r>1$ and by the induction hypothesis, any chain of length $r-1$ connecting any two semistable bundles on $C\times {\rm Spec \,} K$ can be joined by an $\#A^1$-chain of semistable bundles parametrized by $\#A^1_K$.
        
        Consider the first two intersecting families $\@E_1$ and $\@E_2.$  There are two possibilities: they intersect in a semistable bundle or an unstable bundle. In the case that these intersect in a semistable bundle, then applying~\Cref{lem:modify-1-family} to the first chain and applying the induction hypothesis to the remaining chain proves the claim.

        In the case these intersect in an unstable bundle, applying~\Cref{lem:modif-2-family} to $\@E_1$ and $\@E_2$, we get semistable bundle $\~{\@E_1}$ and not-necessarily semi-stable bundle $\~{\@E_2}$ which intersect in a semi-stable bundle say $F$. Then $F$ is connected to $E_2$ by a chain of bundles of length $r-1$, hence by induction $F$ is connected to $E_2$ by a chain of semistable bundles. Hence we are done in this case as well.

body_md: Since $g\ge 2$ and $k$ is infinite, by \cite[Lemma 1.5]{Hof07}, the open substack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ admits a $k$-rational point. The corollary follows from~\Cref{thm:main-text-ss}.

title: Remark
body_md: In the case the genus is 0, the moduli stack $Bun^{ss}_{n, L}$ may or may not admit a $k$-rational point, for example $Bun^{ss}_{n, L, \#P^1}(k)$ is non-empty iff $n\mid \deg L$. Also by~\cite{Tu93}, in case genus of $C$ is 1, and $k=\-k$, $Bun^{ss}_{n, L, C}(k)\neq \emptyset.$

title: Proof
body_md:
In view of~\Cref{lem:a1-chain-a1-conn}, it is enough to show that the corresponding stacks are $\#A^1$-chain connected. 

    We show for each $n\geq 1,$ (1) implies (2) and (2) implies (3). Then we show (1) for each $n$ by induction on $n.$ 
\medskip\\
\noindent\_{\bf Step 1}: We show (1) implies (2). 
Let $K$ be a finitely generated field extension of $k$ and let  $[E_1], [E_2]$ be $K$-points of the moduli stack $\@Sub_{1, I, 2n}(\@E^{univ})$. Consider the morphism $$\Psi_I: \@Sub_{1, I, 2n}(\@E^{univ})\to \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$$ and 
 for $i=1, 2$ the images $\Psi_I([E_i])$ of the corresponding $K$-valued points of $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$. 

Assume $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$ is naively $\#A^1$-chain connected, hence we can assume WLOG that there is $$h: \#A^1_K\to \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$$ such that $h(i): {\rm Spec \,} K\to   \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$ corresponds to $\Psi_I([E_i])$ for $i=1, 2.$ 
    Let $h$ correspond the classifying morphism $c_{\@H}:  \#A^1_K \to \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$ corresponding to an object $$(\@F, \ c: \@F\otimes \@F\to \@L, \ 0\to \@I\to \@H\to \@F\to 0)$$ where $\@F$ is a symplectic bundle and also $\@L$, $\@I$ are line bundles on $C\times_k \#A^1_K$ and $$0\to \@I\to \@H\to \@F\to 0$$ is an extension of vector bundles on $C\times_k \#A^1_K$.  
    Consider the corresponding extension $$0\to \@F^{dual}\otimes \@L \to \@H^{dual}\otimes\@L\to \@I^{dual}\otimes\@L \to 0.$$ 
    Consider $\@M:=\@Ext(\@I^{dual}\otimes \@L, \@H\xrightarrow{c^{\sharp}\circ p} \@F^{dual}\otimes \@L)/\@H^{dual}\otimes\@L$, the moduli stack over $\#A^1_K$ where for any $\#A^1_K$-scheme $S$ the corresponding groupoid $\@M(S)$ consists of objects         $$ \xymatrix{
    0 \ar[r] & \pi^*(\@H) \ar[d]^{\pi^*(c^{\sharp}\circ p)}\ar[r] \ar[d] & \~{\@E} \ar[r] \ar[d] & \pi^*(\@I^{dual}\otimes\@L) \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & 0 \\
    0\ar[r] & \pi^*(\@F^{dual}\otimes \@L) \ar[r] & \pi^*(\@H^{dual}\otimes\@L) \ar[r] & \pi^*(\@I^{dual}\otimes\@L) \ar[r] & 0 
    }$$ where  $\pi: C\times_k S\to C\times_k \#A^1_K$ and, the top row is an exact sequence of vector bundles  over $C\times_k S$. 
    
    By~\cite[Proof of Corollary 3.9]{BH08}, there is a cartesian square $$\xymatrix{
    \@M \ar[r] \ar[d] &  \@Sub_{1, I, 2n}(\@E^{univ}) \ar[d]^{\Psi_I} \\
    \#A^1_K \ar[r]^-{c_{\@H}}  & \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2) 
    }$$ of moduli stacks. 
   Lifting the points $[E_i]$ of the moduli stack $\@Sub_{1, I, 2n}(\@E^{univ})$ to $K$-points $e_i$ of the moduli stack $\@M$ respectively, where $e_1$ lies over $0: {\rm Spec \,} K\to \#A^1_K$ and $1: {\rm Spec \,} K\to \#A^1_K$. Now it is enough to show that the $K$-points $e_1, e_2$ of $\@M$ are naively $\#A^1$-chain connected.  

   By \cite[Definition 3.6, (6)]{BH08}, there is a cartesian square of canonical 1-morphisms $$\xymatrix{
   \@M \ar[r]^-{\phi} \ar[d] & \@Ext(\@I^{dual}\otimes\@L, \@H)  \ar[d]^{(c^{\sharp}\circ p)_*} \\ 
   \#A^1_K\ar[r] &  \@Ext(\@I^{dual}\otimes\@L,\@F^{dual}\otimes \@L)
   }$$ 
   where the right vertical morphism is a morphism of moduli stacks over $\#A^1_K.$ 
Now we are done by taking $\~{\@K}=\@H, \@K=\@F^{dual}\otimes \@L,$ and $ \@Q=\@I^{dual}\otimes\@L$ in~\Cref{prop:ext}.   
\\
\medskip
\noindent   \_{\bf Step 2}: We show (2) implies (3).

 Let $K$ be a finitely generated field extension over $k$  and $[E_1], [E_2]$ be two $K$-valued points of the moduli stack $Sympl_{2n, L}$ corresponding to symplectic bundles $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively, on $C_K=C\times_k{\rm Spec \,} K$. By choosing a line bundle $I$ of deg $\ll0$, we can assume $I$ is a sub-bundle of both $E_1$ and $E_2.$ Hence $[E_1]$ and $[E_2]$ are in the image of the morphism of moduli stacks $$\@Sub_{1, I, 2n}(\@E^{univ})\to Sympl_{2n, L}$$ again denoted by $[E_i]=(E_i, b_i: E_i\otimes E_i\to L, I\subset E_i)$ for $i=1, 2$.   Now by (2) we are done.
\medskip\\
 \noindent    \_{\bf Step 3}: We show (1) by induction on $n\geq 1$. 

 For $n=1$ we have the isomorphisms, $Sympl_{0, L}\simeq {\rm Spec \,} k$ and $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 0)\simeq B\#G_m$ which is naively $\#A^1$-chain connected. 
 
 Assume $n>1$ and by induction hypothesis for $n-1$, $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-4)$ is naively $\#A^1$-chain connected.  
  By the induction hypothesis, and by (2) implies (3), we have that $Sympl_{2n-2, L}$ is naively $\#A^1$-chain connected. Consider the morphism $$\Phi'_I: \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)\to Sympl_{2n-2, L}.$$ 
Let $[\@H_i]=(\@F_i, c_i: \@F_i\otimes \@F_i\to \@L, 0\to\@I_i \to \@H_i \to \@F_i\to 0)$ for $i=1, 2$ be two objects of the groupoid $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)({\rm Spec \,} K)$. Let $$[\@I_i\oplus \@F_i]:=(\@F_i, c_i: \@F_i\otimes \@F_i\to \@L, 0\to\@I_i \to \@I_i\oplus \@F_i\to \@F_i\to 0)$$ for each $i=1, 2$. 
Then for each fixed $i$, there is an inclusion of moduli functors $$\@Ext(\@F_i, \@I_i) \to \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$$ so that the image contains the $K$-points $[\@H_i]$ and $[\@I_i\oplus \@F_i]$. 
By \cite[Proposition 3.1]{Lan83}, the moduli stack $\@Ext(\@F_i, \@I_i)$ is represented by a vector bundle, hence naively $\#A^1$-chain connected and in particular, $[\@H_i]$ and $[\@I_i\oplus \@F_i] $ are naively $\#A^1$-chain connected in $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2).$


Consider the morphism of moduli stacks $$s_I:  Sympl_{2n-2, L}\to \@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)$$ which is defined on groupoids for each $k$-scheme $S$ as follows $$(\@F, c:\@F\otimes \@F\to \@L)\mapsto (\@F, c:\@F\otimes \@F\to \@L, 0\to \pi^*I\to \pi^*I\oplus\@F\to\@F \to 0)$$  where $\pi: C\times S\to C$ is the projection morphism. The morphism $s_I$ is a section of $\Phi'_I.$ 

Clearly the $K$-valued points $[\@I_i\oplus \@F_i]$ are in the image of the morphism $s_I$ for $i=1, 2$ and since as noted before the moduli stack $Sympl_{2n-2, L}$ is naively $\#A^1$-chain connected, the points $[\@I_1\oplus \@F_1]$ and $[\@I_2\oplus \@F_2]$ in the groupoid $\@Ext(\@F^{univ}, I, 2n-2)({\rm Spec \,} K)$ are naively $\#A^1$-chain homotopic. Hence we are done.

title: Definition
body_md:
(\cite[Definition 3.1.1]{AM11})
    We say two smooth proper $k$-schemes $X_0, X_1$ are directly $\#A^1$-h-cobordant if there is a smooth $k$-scheme with a morphism $f: X\to \#A^1$ such that 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $f^{-1}(0)$ is isomorphic to $X_0$ and $f^{-1}(1)$ is isomorphic to $X_1$ and
        \item the natural inclusions $X_i\to X$ are $\#A^1$-equivalences for $i=0,1$.
    \end{enumerate}

    We say $X_0, X_1$ are $\#A^1$-h-cobordant if they are equivalent by the relation generated by the relation of direct $\#A^1$-h-cobordance.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an infinite field $k$. Let $(\@E, b: \@E\otimes \@E\to \@L_1)$ and $(\@F, c: \@F\otimes \@F\to \@L_2)$ be symplectic vector bundles of rank $2n$ on $C$. Let $X=\#P(\@E)$ and $Y=\#P(\@F)$ be the associated projective bundles. Consider the following statements.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $X$ and $Y$ are $\#A^1$-equivalent.
        \item $X$ and Y are $\#A^1$-h-cobordant. 
        \item  $\det \@E \otimes (\det\@F)^{-1}=\@L^{\otimes 2n}$ for some $\@L\in {\rm Pic}(C).$
\item[(3')] $\@L_1 \otimes \@L_2^{-1} = \@N^{\otimes 2}$ for some $\@N \in {\rm Pic}(C)$.
     \end{enumerate}

     Then \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
     \item $(1)\mbox{ $\Longleftrightarrow$ } (2) \mbox{ $\Longleftrightarrow$ } $(3). 
            \item $(3')\Rightarrow (1)$
    \item  if $n\geq 1$ is odd, then $(3) \mbox{ $\Longleftrightarrow$ } (3')$. 
     
     \end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md: The proof follows from \cite[Theorem 1.2]{HY24} by simply observing that the condition (3) in \cite[Theorem 1.2]{HY24} translates into $\@L_1^{\otimes n}\otimes  \@L_2^{\otimes -n}=\@L^{\otimes 2n}$ in ${\rm Pic} (C)$ for some $\@L\in {\rm Pic}(C)$. In other words,  $\@L_1\otimes  \@L_2^{\otimes -1}\otimes \@L^{\otimes -n}$ is of order $n$ in ${\rm Pic}(C).$ But $n$ is odd, hence $\@L_1\otimes  \@L_2^{\otimes -1}\otimes \@L^{\otimes -2}\simeq \@L'^{\otimes 2}$ for some $\@L'\in{\rm Pic} (C).$ Hence $\@L_1\otimes  \@L_2^{\otimes -1}\simeq \@N^{\otimes 2}$ for $\@N=\@L\otimes \@L'.$

label: def:q-parabolic-sympl
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:q-parabolic-sympl} Fix a line bundle $L$ on $C$ and a quasi-parabolic data $(e, \_m)$ on $C$ of rank $2n$ along $D$. 

For any $k$-scheme $S$ and the projection $\pi: C\times_k S\to C$, a quasi-Parabolic symplectic bundle of rank $2n$ parametrized by $S$ of quasi-parabolic data $(e, \_m)$ is given by tuple $(\@E_*, \phi_*, \@L(D))$ where 
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\@E_*$ is a quasi-parabolic bundle parametrized by $S$ in the sense of \Cref{def:q-parabolic}.
    \item $\@L$ a line bundle on $C\times_k S$, Zariski locally on $S$ isomorphic to $\pi^*L$ where $\pi:C\times_k S\to C$ is the projection.
    
    $\@L(D)$ denotes the quasi-parabolic bundle parametrized by $S$, 
    given by the line bundle $\@L$ with the special quasi-parabolic structure, {\it i.e.\/},\  $e(p)=1$ for all $p\in D.$ 
    \item an anti-symmetric morphism of parabolic bundles $$\phi_*: \@E_*\otimes \@E_*\to \@L(D)$$
    such that the induced morphism 
    $$\~{\phi}: \@E_*= \@E_* \otimes \@O_{C\times S} \to  \@E_*\otimes (\@E_* \otimes \@E^{\vee}_*) = (\@E_* \otimes \@E_*) \otimes \@E^{\vee}_*\xrightarrow{\phi\otimes {\rm Id}}  \@L(D) \otimes \@E^{\vee}_*$$
    is an isomorphism.
\end{itemize}

title: Proof
body_md:
We note the following fiber product diagram of stacks $$\xymatrix{
    qPSympl^{e, \_m}_{2n, L}\ar[d] \ar[r]& qPSympl^{e, \_m}_{2n} \ar[d] \\
    Sympl_{2n, L} \ar[r] & Sympl_{2n}}$$
where the vertical maps are forgetful morphisms (forgetting the quasi-parabolic structure). To see that the right vertical map is well defined, the proof in~\cite[Lemma 3.1]{BCD26} works in our setting. Recall that the right vertical map is given by $$(\@E_*, \phi_*: \@E_*\otimes \@E_*\to \@L(D))\mapsto  (\@E, \phi:\@E\otimes \@E\to \@L).$$ It follows that the above diagram is cartesian. 

    By~\cite[Lemma 3.2.2(ii)]{HS10} the right vertical map is Zariski locally trivial with fiber a product of finite flag varieties, hence the same holds for the left vertical map.  Now each Flag variety is $\#A^1$-chain connected and by~\Cref{thm:main}(3), $Sympl_{2n, L}$ is $\#A^1$-connected, hence the moduli stack $qPSympl^{e, \_m}_{2n, L}$ is $\#A^1$-connected.
